doc.title: Houston Person Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 2, 1998 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Working with Etta Jones
summary: Person explains his dream of having a singer, how he and Etta Jones share the set without formal planning, and that they have been together thirty years.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Did it help to add the vocal element to your group from a working standpoint?

Yeah. Well I wanted to have a band with a singer. That was my dream. Because when I used to see the bands come to the south, the bands would always have a singer. So it helped a lot. And having somebody with the stature of Etta wanting to be in the band was great. So it worked out fine. It’s been a great help. It gives more balance for the presentation, so that’s really helped. I hope to bring the group up here some day.
To Hamilton? That sounds like a good idea.
You said that on camera, so—
I’m hustling a gig on camera.
Well I hope to play with your band some day.
How do you guys, you and Etta work out, you both bring tunes to the table and say—

No we don’t work that way. Whatever she wants to do she does, whatever I want to do I do. And then we clash, and, “you take it a little while” and, “I’ll take it a little while.” And sometimes I’ll suggest one that she should do and she’ll say, “oh, no,” then I’ll play
it and she likes it. “Yeah I think I will.” Then I like it. No it’s a lot of fun, but we don’t know, we don’t do any of those things.
You probably had to re-learn some standards in different keys for her voice?
No not really. No. Well I mean I know all the keys anyway.
But no we just, well we’ve been together 30 years.
So this has been worked out long ago, right?
Yeah, just trial and errors over the years, so we just go and do it. Yeah that’s the way it works.
